setup: Hands at your chest or by your sides
execution: Dip into a quarter to half squat
Drive up and jump as high as you can
Land softly on the balls of your feet
Sink into the landing, then reset
faults: Don't let your knees cave in
Don't keep going when the jumps slow down

notes: Jump on a non-slip surface with clear space and enough headroom.
Keep sets short (about 3–5 jumps) and rest fully, so each jump is fast.
Practise landing quietly with knees in line with the toes before jumping for height.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain at the knee, shin or ankle on landing
Pain that changes how you move

keyPositions.label: Dip
keyPositions.describe: Hips back and knees bent into about a half squat, chest up, hands at the chest. Heels down.

keyPositions.label: Air
keyPositions.describe: Hips, knees and ankles fully straightened, feet off the floor, toes pointed down, body upright.

keyPositions.label: Landing
keyPositions.describe: Landing on the balls of the feet and rolling to the whole foot, hips back, knees bent and in line with the toes.

ikHints: Feet return to the same spot
Knees track over the toes on landing
emphasise: Knees in line with the toes
